title: Replacing a class: the singleton decorator

kcs.statement: PEP 318's singleton decorator replaces a class with a function that creates one instance on the first call and returns that same instance on every later call.
Because the singleton decorator rebinds the class name to a function, isinstance(x, Name) raises TypeError and the class can no longer be subclassed by name.

problem_ideas: Implement PEP 318's @singleton and check a() is a() for two calls
Predict the error from isinstance(obj, Config) after @singleton
Rewrite the singleton as a modify-in-place class decorator that keeps the class
Decide whether a module-level instance would be simpler for a config object
Predict what happens to constructor arguments on the second call
Explain why class Child(Config) fails after decoration
